text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Presidential Adviser Osama el-Baz denies that there will be a four-way meeting between Egypt, the Palestinian Authority, the United States and Israel. Baz, who spoke as he was leaving for Oslo, said that his visit to Norway was to discuss bilateral ties and the peace process.
- Investigations will start today on Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi's report on the Al-Shaab newspaper.
- Agricultural land will be made available to those affected by the law on the relationship between farmers and renters.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and Palestinian planning minister Nabil Shaath discuss the future of the peace process and the effect of the Israeli closure on the West Bank and Gaza, as well as the visit to the Middle East of the United States Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi says it has been decided to develop a small oil field in the eastern desert.
- Interpol Egypt detains a Bahraini trader who fled to Egypt after setting a fire in which two people died.
- President Hosni Mubarak will open the second phase of the metro on October 1.
